messages:
sara (support): Heads-up: ACME on dedicated-omega is seeing a throughput drop and 10-20x latency spikes since 09:28 UTC. Frontend shows 429s and heavy queue lengths. Customer is blocked. :frowning:

rahul (oncall): Thanks — tenant_id and model? Any recent config changes or canary?

sara (support): tenant=acme, model=rwx-13b-quant, pool=dedicated-omega, no config updates from them. We did a scheduled autoscaler tweak 08:50 (more burst capacity) but nothing else.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] burst-capacity-change applied to pool dedicated-omega at 2026-03-17T08:50:12Z by infra-bot

elaine (runtime): I pulled metrics: prefill_queue_depth and continuous_batcher.backlog spiked at 09:27. batch_tokens_inflight jumped >3x. Looks like packing efficiency collapsed.

rahul (oncall): Any signs of a noisy tenant? high inflight_concurrency from one tenant?

elaine (runtime): Yes — acme shows many small short-context requests interleaved with a few very long-context requests. Our sorter is mis-prioritizing, so tiny requests get stuck behind huge prefills. That causes the batcher to ramp micro-batches and trigger token-ceil-based flushes => more small batches => worse throughput.

sara (support): Customer logs match: many short 8-32 token calls plus occasional 4096-token previews. They reported this pattern starting after a model quant swap on their side yesterday.

tim (sre): Can we confirm config values? post the current max_batch_tokens and scheduler.sort_mode for that pool.

elaine (runtime): Pulled from /configs/runtime/dedicated-omega:
```
max_batch_tokens: "8192"
scheduler:
  sort_mode: "none"
  inflight_concurrency_limit: 256
  prefill_timeout_ms: 60
```
Sort_mode==none is the problem — we used to have length-sort canary, it got reverted in the 08:50 autoscale push.

rahul (oncall): Repro steps to validate locally?

elaine (runtime): Repro on staging:
1) spawn workload: 600rps with 80% short (8-32 tokens) + 20% long (2k-4k).
2) enable continuous-batcher with sort_mode=\"none\" and max_batch_tokens=8192.
3) observe batch size distribution and latency. Expect tiny batches and >2kms tail.

curl example for metrics:
```
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=continuous_batcher_batch_tokens_inflight{pool=\"dedicated-omega\"}" | jq .
```
pprof capture:
```
kubectl exec -c runtime pod/serve-omega-1 -- go tool pprof http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=20
```

ops-bot: [incident] creating incident INC-2251 (throughput drop — dedicated-omega) assigned to eng-runtime

tim (sre): Immediate mitigation options:
- flip scheduler.sort_mode back to "length_desc" for dedicated-omega (hotfix)
- lower max_batch_tokens to 4096 temporarily to avoid huge prefill stalls
- apply tenant rate-limit for acme if they keep sending long tails
I'll take the hotfix, can someone run the config patch?

rahul (oncall): On it. Applying sort_mode=length_desc now (canary to 2 nodes).

elaine (runtime): Patch applied to canary pods. Observability: small batch count dropping, median latency improving in 30s. Keeping an eye on tail.

sara (support): Customer reports partial improvement — some endpoints back to normal, still occasional 429s but much better. They patched their quant swap too. :relieved:

tim (sre): Next steps: schedule a full rollout of sorter fix, add a regression test for packing efficiency (short+long mixes), and add alert for sudden collapse in batch_size_variance. Also verify autoscaler pushes don't remove sorter config again.

elaine (runtime): Filed RFC to make sorter config immutable per pool unless explicitly changed by runtime-ops. Also adding a metric and chart for max_batch_tokens utilization.

rahul (oncall): Closing INC-2251 when rollout completes and 1hr stable. Thanks all :thumbsup:
